title: Fix a dripping bathroom sink faucet
summary: Disassemble a two-handle bathroom sink faucet to replace the worn cartridge, spring and rubber seat that cause dripping. Shut off the water supply valves under the sink first to avoid flooding.

steps.title: Turn off water supply
steps.instruction: Reach under the sink and turn the water supply valve clockwise until it stops. Repeat for the other side if needed.
steps.done_when: both supply valves under the sink are fully closed and no water flows

steps.title: Remove faucet handle
steps.instruction: Insert the hex key into the set screw on the side of the handle and loosen it. Lift the handle straight off.
steps.done_when: the handle is lifted off and the white stem is exposed

steps.title: Remove packing nut
steps.instruction: Fit the adjustable wrench on the packing nut and turn counterclockwise to loosen it. Unscrew the nut the rest of the way by hand and remove it.
steps.done_when: the packing nut is free from the faucet body

steps.title: Pull out cartridge
steps.instruction: Grip the white plastic stem and pull straight up to lift the cartridge out of the faucet body.
steps.done_when: the cartridge is out and the valve cavity is empty

steps.title: Extract seat and spring
steps.instruction: Use a small pick to hook the black rubber seat in the valve cavity and pull it out. Hook the metal spring underneath and pull it out.
steps.done_when: the old seat and spring are out and set aside for matching

steps.title: Install new spring and gasket
steps.instruction: Drop the new spring into the hole in the faucet body. Press the new black rubber gasket over it so it seats flat.
steps.done_when: the new spring and rubber seat sit down in the valve cavity

quote.text: Now it's time to install the new spring and gasket in place.

steps.title: Insert cartridge and tighten nut
steps.instruction: Push the new cartridge down into the faucet body. Thread the packing nut on by hand, then tighten it securely with the adjustable wrench.
steps.done_when: the cartridge is seated and the packing nut is tight and secure

quote.text: Insert the new cartridge, reinstall the packing nut and tighten tighten it securely

steps.title: Reattach handle and restore water
steps.instruction: Set the handle back on the stem and tighten its set screw with the hex key. Reach under the sink and turn the supply valve back on.
steps.done_when: the handle is fixed on the stem and the supply valves are open

quote.text: reattach the handle and turn back on the on the water.

steps.title: Test for drips
steps.instruction: Turn the handle on to flush, then turn it fully off. Watch the spout to confirm there is no drip.
steps.done_when: the faucet shuts off fully with no drip from the spout
